name: Xbox 360 Controller
notes: XInput/Xbox360. PID is 0x02FF (Xbox One wired family), DELIBERATELY != the real Xbox360 wired 0x028E. VID stays 0x045E so it works as XInput (the companion's rumble/state gates check VendorId only, never PID) and ControllerKind::detect maps any 045E to XInput; both devnodes bind via their generic fallback hardware ids (root\HIDMaestro, root\HIDMaestroXUSB) regardless of PID. The 0x02FF PID's PURPOSE is read-side identification: FlexInput's gilrs read side identifies OUR virtual by VID/PID 045E:02FF OR a name containing 'hidmaestro' (see gilrs_backend::is_hidmaestro_virtual_xinput). INPUT goes through the XUSB companion via the SHM GipData[14] region encoded by encode::gip_from_state -- the SWD companion is the SOLE game-visible identity (it publishes the {EC87F1E3} XUSB interface that xinput1_4/Steam read; WGI shows it as 'HIDMaestro XInput Companion' 045E:02FF). The main HID node exists only to host the driver config/SHM plumbing, and its descriptor is a VENDOR-DEFINED usage page (0xFF00, 12 opaque bytes to match inputReportSize) so NO game API ever enumerates it as a gamepad. History: it used to carry a real gamepad TLC (DirectInput face). Win10's WGI hid that face (single-pad view), but two Win11 mechanisms surfaced it as a SECOND pad: (1) Win11's xinputhid.inf exact-matches HID\VID_045E&PID_02FF&IG_00 and binds xinputhid.sys, publishing a phantom second XInput slot (dodged by the IG_01 tag -- see orchestrator::create_device_node); (2) Win11 26H1's GameInput-backed WGI stopped hiding IG_-tagged HID gamepads, so the face showed up in WGI/Steam as a live 'Xbox One Controller' next to the companion (groundtruthed on build 28000). Vendor usage kills both classes of leak deterministically, at the cost of the (marginal) DirectInput face -- DI-only titles should use the DS4 profile instead. gilrs_backend::disposition_for additionally Drops any non-companion 045E:02FF pad, which covers still-deployed nodes created with the old gamepad descriptor.
